terra.problem: Calling Jeremiah 'not a diplomat' asserts a role he did not have without support from the passage.
'Zedekiah's men knew a prophet's job, and so should we' adds an unsupported claim about what the men knew and sounds preachy toward the baker.
The oven mitt turning on him is an unclear comparison to weapons being turned against people in war.
The verse says the Chaldeans besiege the city outside the wall; it does not say they are camped there.
The cookie sheet and brick wall comparison does not match the action in the passage or make a clear joke.
Papa comments on his own telling when he says he is not going to tell a joke.
'Judah is where they already are, and that's the problem' adds an unsupported explanation for their situation.
'We'll just read it plainly' comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
The flood and bakery line has no clear connection to the action in the passage and makes a joke beside the city's destruction.
'I'll stay with the words as they're written' comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
'I'll leave them as they stand' comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
The explanation states that the people feel safe without marking their feeling as Papa's guess.
The passage directs the message to the king, officials and people, but does not say they are all hearing it together.
The passage directs the message to the king, officials and people; it does not say they heard it.
'Nobody moves in' asserts an outcome beyond the warning that the house will become rubble.
The vineyard punchline does not work: vines can be cut down, so the comparison rests on a false distinction.
